# `nlink-lab events`

## Reference

<!-- cli-ref:start (generated by `nlink-lab docs-gen`; do not edit) -->

```text
Show a lab's lifecycle log (deploy, apply, spawn, kill, impair, partition, snapshot, …); `--follow` merges live drift (RTNETLINK / nftables) and runtime (process exit, link state) events, optionally fanned out on a unix socket.

JSON OUTPUT (with `--json`): one record per line tagged `source: lifecycle | drift | runtime`. Schema: docs/json-schemas/events.schema.json

Usage: nlink-lab events [OPTIONS] <LAB>

Arguments:
  <LAB>
          Lab name

Options:
  -f, --follow
          Keep running: tail new lifecycle events and merge live drift (`watch`) and runtime events (process exits, interface state). Drift and runtime sources need root; without it only the lifecycle log is followed

      --since <DURATION>
          Only events newer than this (`10m`, `2h`, `30s`)

      --kind <KIND>
          Only these event kinds (repeatable): lifecycle names such as `deployed`, `impaired`, `spawned`, or the sources `lifecycle`, `drift`, `runtime`

      --interval <INTERVAL>
          Runtime-event sampling interval in seconds (with --follow)
          
          [default: 2]

      --socket <PATH>
          Also serve the stream on a unix socket: every client that connects receives one NDJSON record per line (with --follow)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

<!-- cli-ref:end -->
